issues.legal_issue: A collusive consent decree obtained by the vendor and purchasers after a pre-emption action begins does not bind the pre-emption claimants.
material_facts: After the pre-emption action began, the vendor and purchasers obtained a consent decree that the courts of fact found collusive.
The pre-emption claimants were not parties to that decree.
issues.conclusion: The collusive decree could not bind the pre-emption claimants.
issues.legal_principle: A collusive decree between the vendor and purchasers cannot defeat the rights of pre-emption claimants who are not bound by it. The judgment relies on no earlier cases or statutory provision for this proposition.

predicates.preemption_action: A claimant has brought an action to enforce a right of pre-emption.
predicates.post_suit_collusive_consent_decree: After the pre-emption action began, the vendor and purchaser obtained a consent decree found to be collusive.

issues.definition: When a pre-emption action is pending and the vendor and purchaser obtain a collusive consent decree afterward, that decree does not bind the pre-emption claimants.

issues.legal_issue: A pre-emption claim may succeed where a real sale is found and the asserted ground that the sale was void was neither put in issue nor proved.
material_facts: The claimants brought a pre-emption action based on a registered deed purporting to convey the land absolutely.
The defence asserted that the land was ancestral and that a local custom prevented its alienation without family necessity.
The alleged custom was not proved, and the asserted voidness of the sale was not made the subject of an issue.
The courts found that a real sale had occurred.
issues.conclusion: The finding that there had been a real sale was correct, and the claimants were entitled to succeed on their pre-emption claim.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 4 of the Punjab Pre-emption Act, 1913, a real sale gives rise to the asserted pre-emption claim. A defence that an alienation was void cannot defeat that claim where the asserted ground was not put in issue and the alleged custom was not proved. The judgment relies on no earlier cases.

rule.if: preemption_action and sale_found_real and (voidness_issue_not_framed or alleged_custom_not_proved)

predicates.preemption_action: A claimant has brought an action to enforce a right of pre-emption.
predicates.sale_found_real: The court finds that the transfer was a real sale.
predicates.voidness_issue_not_framed: The asserted ground that the sale was void was not made the subject of an issue.
predicates.alleged_custom_not_proved: The party relying on an alleged custom to invalidate the sale did not prove that custom.

issues.definition: A pre-emption claim succeeds when a real sale is found and the asserted ground for treating it as void was either not put in issue or not proved.

issues.legal_issue: A real sale does not cease to support a pre-emption claim merely because it was made to evade land-reform legislation.
material_facts: The vendor transferred the land to close relations at a concessional rate.
The transaction may have been intended to avoid the effect of impending land-ceiling legislation.
The court treated the transaction as a real sale.
issues.conclusion: The motive for the transaction did not alter the fact that it was a sale, and the pre-emption claimants were entitled to succeed.
issues.legal_principle: The court determines the pre-emption claim by the fact of the sale, not by the motive behind it. An attempt to defeat land-reform legislation through a sale still involves a real sale where the transaction is found to be real. The judgment relies on no earlier cases.

predicates.preemption_action: A claimant has brought an action to enforce a right of pre-emption.
predicates.sale_found_real: The court finds that the transfer was a real sale.
predicates.sale_made_to_evade_land_reform: The seller made the sale in an effort to avoid the effects of land-reform legislation.

issues.definition: When a real sale made to avoid land-reform legislation is the subject of a pre-emption action, the motive does not prevent a pre-emption right from arising from the sale.

issues.legal_issue: A claimant's untrue testimony does not require dismissal of a suit that is otherwise entitled to succeed.
material_facts: The claimant's evidence was not frank or straightforward.
The courts had found that the claimant was otherwise entitled to succeed on the pre-emption claim.
issues.conclusion: The claim was not to be dismissed as a penalty for the claimant's untrue testimony.
issues.legal_principle: The penalty for untrue testimony is not dismissal of a suit that otherwise has to be decreed. The judgment relies on no earlier cases or statutory provision for this proposition.

predicates.suit_otherwise_entitled_to_decree: The court finds that the claimant's suit is otherwise entitled to succeed.
predicates.claimant_gave_untrue_testimony: The claimant gave testimony that was untrue or not frank and straightforward.

issues.definition: When a claimant gives untrue testimony but the suit is otherwise entitled to succeed, the suit is not dismissed on that ground.

issues.legal_issue: Where both sides have unclean hands, each side may be ordered to bear its own costs throughout the proceedings.
material_facts: The court considered the conduct of both sides to show unclean hands.
issues.conclusion: Each side was ordered to bear its own costs throughout the proceedings.
issues.legal_principle: The court denied costs to both sides because the circumstances showed unclean hands on both sides. The judgment relies on no earlier cases or statutory provision for this costs order.

predicates.both_sides_unclean_hands: The court finds that both sides have acted with unclean hands in the proceedings.

issues.definition: When both sides have unclean hands and the appeal is dismissed, each side bears its own costs.
